programme.how_found: site:uct.ac.za search 'UCT Faculty of Science BSc Computer Science undergraduate programme' -> uct.ac.za Science: undergraduate page; programme code from the 2027 Directions for Undergraduate Applicants PDF; major structure from the 2026 Faculty of Science Handbook (Handbook 11) linked from uct.ac.za/students/study-uct-handbooks/handbooks.
programme.notes: UCT has no stand-alone 'BSc in Computer Science' degree page: Computer Science is a major (CSC05) within the 3-year BSc (SB001). Teaching language English is inferred from UCT's university-wide English-proficiency requirement and 'English medium-of-instruction' wording; no page states 'taught in English' for this major specifically. Campus is inferred from the Faculty office/Computer Science Building location on Upper Campus. The 2027 Science handbook was not yet linked; the 2026 handbook was used.

english.quote: IELTS: A valid (no more than 2 years old) IELTS Academic Test Report Form with an overall score of band 6.5 or above, with at least 6.0 in each component.

supporting_quotes.quote: Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL): A valid (no more than 2 years old) TOEFL iBT Score Report with an overall score of 88 or above, with at least 19 in Listening, 19 in Writing, 20 in Reading and 22 in Speaking.
If you are writing an English proficiency test you must ensure that the results are submitted to the Admissions Office by 1 October 2026.
An overall band score of 7.0 (with no individual element of the test scoring below 6.0) on the International English Language Testing System (IELTS)

english.how_found: site:uct.ac.za search for international undergraduate English requirements -> Language requirements page; cross-checked verbatim against the 2027 Directions for Undergraduate Applicants PDF (same IELTS/TOEFL/PTE figures).
english.notes: Applies because a Kazakhstan NIS applicant's school is not English-medium/English is not a home language (the requirement applies to 'All international students for whom English is not a first/home language...'). CONFLICT: the older '2026 Guidelines for Holders of International School-Leaving Certificates' PDF, Faculty of Science page, still lists IELTS 7.0 (no band below 6.0), TOEFL iBT 88 and PTE 64. The current university-wide page and the 2027 Directions both give IELTS 6.5/6.0; the live page also says 'For programme-specific requirements, please consult the relevant Faculty handbook' -- applicant should confirm with the Science Faculty whether 7.0 still applies. Results due by 1 October 2026 (the 2027 Directions key-dates timeline shows 30 Sept).

value.description: No published threshold for a Kazakhstan (NIS Grade 12) school-leaving certificate. UCT publishes a Faculty of Science FPS of 34+ (best five subjects) and subject minima only for CAIE, NSSC and IB; all other international qualifications are assessed individually (curriculum, academic performance, NBTs where appropriate). Eligibility for South African matriculation exemption (USAf Matriculation Board) is also required.

gpa.quote: Should you hold a school-leaving certificate for which admission criteria are not specified in the 2027 Undergraduate Prospectus, your application will be considered individually, taking into account your school curriculum, academic performance and National Benchmark Test results, where appropriate.

supporting_quotes.quote: Admission to the Faculty of Science requires an applicant to have achieved a FPS of 34 points or above, based on the five best subjects (including the required subjects).
Applicants writing other international authority examinations will be assessed on their individual merits.
NOTE: Due to capacity constraints offers are unlikely to be made to applicants who only meet the minimum admission requirements.
If you have a school-leaving certificate from an international or foreign examining authority, you must consult the Matriculation Board to establish if you are eligible for matriculation exemption

gpa.how_found: 2027 Directions for Undergraduate Applicants (admission requirements section) and the 2026 Guidelines for Holders of International School-Leaving Certificates PDF (Faculty of Science page) found via site:uct.ac.za search.
gpa.notes: Kazakhstan / NIS is not among the qualifications in UCT's international guidelines (only CAIE, NSSC, IB and SAT tables). BSc subject expectations for listed systems include strong Mathematics and Physical Science (e.g. IB Maths AA HL5/SL6). The Computer Science department's own page mentions 70% NSC Mathematics 'or equivalent' (search snippet only, not verified on a read page). No 2027 version of the international guidelines PDF was found; the 2026 edition was used.

supporting_quotes.quote: International applicants who are not taking the South African NSC must ensure that predicted scores are submitted by 31 October 2026.

deadline.how_found: site:uct.ac.za search 'UCT undergraduate application closing date 2027 international applicants' -> 2027 Directions for Undergraduate Applicants PDF, 'Dates by which to apply' section.
deadline.notes: Intake Feb 2027 = South African academic year 2027, which is the intake an applicant applying now targets; the 2027 cycle is published. The application deadline (31 July 2026) has ALREADY PASSED as of 2026-10-17; the next possible intake is 2028 (applications typically open 1 April of the preceding year). The 2027 Directions key-dates timeline also lists: supporting documents for international applicants and English proof due 30 Sept 2026 (incomplete applications cancelled by 15 Nov), and 15 Nov 2026 as the deadline for international applicants to attract an offer.

tuition.how_found: site:uct.ac.za search 'UCT international student fees 2027 undergraduate science faculty term fee' -> 2026 Student Fees booklet (section 2.1 Typical First Year Tuition Fees and International Term Fee section) and 2027 Fees and Payment Dates PDF linked from the Fees handbook page.
tuition.notes: Derived figure: UCT charges per course, so there is no single published BSc tuition for internationals. 167,400 = 2026 typical first-year BSc fee R87,000 (stated as 'for South African applicants'; varies with course choice) + 2026 International Term Fee for Bachelors, students from outside Africa (Kazakhstan) ZAR 80,400. 2026 is the latest full fee schedule published; the 2027 Student Fees Handbook is not yet out (the 2027 payment-dates sheet says it will be available towards the end of 2026). For 2027 only the minimum first payment before registration is published: R127,400 for full-time international fee-paying students ('This is not the full cost'). Excludes residence, application fee (non-SADC) and medical aid. In the 2027 Directions quote the trailing '3' is a footnote marker; the list continues '(ii) the International Administrative Service Fee, and (iii) an international faculty term fee.'

scholarship_exists.quote: Unless otherwise stated, eligibility for all Entrance Scholarships is restricted to South African citizens and to South African permanent residents.

supporting_quotes.quote: (note that a limited number of scholarships will be reserved for top South African students writing international examinations)

A small portion of the faculty’s allotted amount for Faculty Entrance Scholarships is set aside to be awarded at the dean’s discretion and may be used for awards to applicants holding international school-leaving qualifications.
South African citizens and permanent residents are eligible for these awards.

scholarship_exists.how_found: site:uct.ac.za searches for undergraduate scholarships for international students -> DSA Entrance Scholarships page (2027 thresholds), Funding & fees FAQ, Undergraduate Bursaries and Loans booklet 2026, Postgraduate international and refugee scholarships page.
scholarship_exists.notes: No named university-run scholarship open to an incoming non-South-African BSc applicant was found. The Faculty of Science 2027 entrance scholarships are for 'South African applicants' (FPS 720+, NSC Maths 85%+). The only opening is the generic dean's-discretion portion of Faculty Entrance Scholarships, which 'may be used' for holders of international school-leaving qualifications -- unnamed, not guaranteed, and in Science the international-exam allocation is reserved for South Africans. UCT's 'International and refugee scholarships' are postgraduate only and the 2026 call did not open due to funding constraints. A search snippet mentioned the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at UCT (undergraduate, closed 30 Sept 2026); not read and generally aimed at African students, so not counted.

scholarship_international.quote: Unless otherwise stated, eligibility for all Entrance Scholarships is restricted to South African citizens and to South African permanent residents.
scholarship_international.how_found: Same DSA Entrance Scholarships page (general conditions and Faculty of Science section).
scholarship_international.notes: False for a Kazakhstan national in Science: the restriction applies, and the Science section names only South African applicants. Caveat: the dean's discretionary portion 'may be used for awards to applicants holding international school-leaving qualifications' (not explicitly limited by citizenship), so a small discretionary award cannot be fully ruled out.
